# Rules reference

<!-- generated by tools/gen_rules_doc.py — do not edit by hand -->

Every finding names a rule id. The **FP rate** column is the false-positive rate the scanner itself
reports for the rule: measured on a corpus by `tools/measure_fp.py`, or **not measured** — never an
estimate. A measured rate is the share of clean projects (that gave the rule something to judge) on
which it fired anyway.

Severities are defaults; `aibom.policy.yaml` decides which ones fail the build (`fail_on`).

## Packages

| Rule | Severity | FP rate | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ait.pkg.malicious` | critical | not measured | The exact version is a known-malicious release (OSV `MAL-`, SecDB). Only an expiring suppression naming the fingerprint accepts it. |
| `ait.pkg.malicious-range` | medium | not measured | The declared range admits a known-malicious version; pin outside it. |
| `ait.pkg.malicious-unpinned` | low | not measured | No exact version, and some version of this package is known-malicious. |
| `ait.pkg.nonexistent` | high | not measured | The name does not exist on PyPI/npm — a hallucinated or slopsquat-able dependency. |
| `ait.pkg.security-holder` | critical | not measured | npm replaced the package with a security holder: it was malicious. |
| `ait.pkg.new-package` | medium | not measured | First published in the last 72 hours. |
| `ait.pkg.version-missing` | medium | not measured | The pinned version does not exist on the registry (yanked or never published). |
| `ait.pkg.typosquat` | medium | 0.20 % (n=1017) | The name looks like a widely used or AI package: a separator change, lookalike letters (rn for m), a swapped, missing, doubled or adjacent-key letter. A name one keystroke from a 4-letter popular name counts only when the registry shows it is under a year old. |
| `ait.pkg.dormant-release` | medium | 0.00 % (n=131) | The release in use is under 30 days old and came after two years or more with no release: a sign of a taken-over account. |
| `ait.pkg.version-jump` | medium | 0.00 % (n=131) | The release in use is under 30 days old and its major version is 10 or more above every earlier release (1.x to 99.0.0), as dependency-confusion attacks publish; CalVer years are not jumps. |
| `ait.pkg.provenance-dropped` | medium | 0.00 % (n=317) | The release in use is under 30 days old and unsigned, though the release before it was signed (a PEP 740 attestation on PyPI; trusted publishing or --provenance on npm): it may have been uploaded with a stolen token, outside the project's CI. |
| `ait.pkg.publisher-change` | medium | 0.63 % (n=317) | The release in use is under 30 days old and came from someone new: on npm a publisher who was neither a maintainer nor the publisher of the release before; on PyPI an attestation from another repository. |
| `ait.pkg.secdb.<verdict>` | varies | not measured | SecDB's verdict for the package (logged in only). |

| Rule | Severity | FP rate | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ext.virustotal.malicious` | high | not measured | VirusTotal's result, not an AIterprise rule (`--byo virustotal=ENV_VAR`): 5 or more engines flag the file's SHA-256 as malicious. See [Third-party providers](providers.md). |
| `ext.virustotal.suspicious` | medium | not measured | VirusTotal's result: 1 to 4 engines flag the file as malicious, or engines flag it as suspicious only — a few engines can be a false positive. |

## Model files

Static analysis only — nothing is unpickled or loaded.

| Rule | Severity | FP rate | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ait.model.pickle.dangerous-global` | critical | not measured | A pickle stream imports a callable on the deny list (process execution, eval/exec, dynamic import, network, native code, destructive filesystem operations or a nested deserializer). Unpickling the file runs that callable. Individual deny entries may lower severity/verdict for serializers that embed code by design (dill, cloudpickle). |
| `ait.model.pickle.unknown-global` | medium | not measured | A pickle stream imports callables that are on neither the deny list nor the known-safe list (often the publisher's own classes from a full-model pickle). Unpickling imports and may call them. Raised to high when the name traverses module attributes (a dotted name through a lower-case segment), a known way to reach a denied callable from an allowed module. |
| `ait.model.pickle.unresolved-global` | high | not measured | A pickle imports a callable whose module or name cannot be determined statically (STACK_GLOBAL operands that are not constant strings, or copyreg extension codes). Legitimate serializers do not produce this; it is a common obfuscation technique. |
| `ait.model.pickle.format` | info | not measured | Pickle-based model file whose imported callables are all on the known-safe list. The format itself still lets a loader execute code, so a future or tampered copy of the same file may not be safe. |
| `ait.model.malformed` | medium | not measured | The container is truncated, corrupt or internally inconsistent (bad pickle bytecode, unreadable ZIP, CRC mismatch, duplicate members, out-of-bounds safetensors header, broken GGUF/ONNX structure, missing signature, or a pickle disguised with a non-executable format's extension). Loaders differ in how they treat such files, which attackers use to evade scanners; anything found before the error still applies. |
| `ait.model.not-analysable` | medium | not measured | Part or all of the file could not be analysed (LZ4 compression, encrypted or unsupported ZIP members, size/opcode caps reached, unrecognised content). This is not a clean result: the unanalysed part may contain anything. |
| `ait.model.zip-slip` | high | not measured | Archive member names are absolute, carry a drive letter, contain a NUL byte or a `..` segment, so extracting the archive can write outside the target directory (zip slip). |
| `ait.model.gguf.chat-template-ssti` | high | not measured | The GGUF `tokenizer.chat_template` metadata contains Jinja server-side template injection markers (dunder attribute access, popen/subprocess/import). Runtimes that render the template without a sandbox execute code (CVE-2024-34359, llama-cpp-python). |
| `ait.model.onnx.custom-op-domain` | medium | not measured | The ONNX graph uses operators from a non-standard domain (not '', ai.onnx, ai.onnx.ml, ai.onnx.training, ai.onnx.preview.training, a known runtime-vendor domain, or a model-local function domain). Running it requires a custom-operator library, i.e. native code supplied outside the model. |
| `ait.model.onnx.vendor-op-domain` | info | not measured | The ONNX graph uses operators from a known runtime-vendor domain (for example com.microsoft contrib ops built into onnxruntime). Inventory only: the model is tied to that runtime. |
| `ait.model.onnx.external-data-path` | high | not measured | An ONNX tensor's external-data location is absolute or contains `..`, so loading the model reads a file outside the model directory (CVE-2022-25882, CVE-2024-27318). |
| `ait.model.keras.lambda-layer` | high | not measured | The Keras model contains a Lambda layer, which serialises arbitrary Python (marshalled bytecode or a named function) that runs when the model is loaded or called (CVE-2024-3660 for Keras < 2.13). Raised to critical when the base64-decoded bytecode contains names on the token list (never unmarshalled; a byte search only). For HDF5 files the detection is a bounded byte search of the model_config JSON (heuristic). |
| `ait.model.keras.dangerous-callable` | critical | not measured | The Keras v3 config.json references a module/function on the pickle deny list (e.g. module 'os', function 'system'). Keras resolves these when it loads the model, even with safe_mode (CVE-2025-1550). |
| `ait.model.mar.handler-code` | info | not measured | The TorchServe .mar archive ships custom handler Python code that the model server imports and runs when the model is served. |

Matched in MCP server commands, skill scripts and package install scripts. The rule id is `ait.mcp.cmd.<id>`, `ait.skill.cmd.<id>` or `ait.archive.cmd.<id>`. The FP rate is the one measured on agent skills (`ait.skill.cmd.<id>`).

| `download-exec.curl-pipe-python` | download-exec | critical | 0.00 % (n=275) | Downloads remote code and pipes it into a Python interpreter. |

## Poisoned descriptions and instructions

Matched in MCP tool descriptions and agent-skill text. The rule id is `ait.mcp.desc.<id>` or `ait.skill.desc.<id>`. The FP rate is the one measured on agent skills (`ait.skill.desc.<id>`), whose long bodies are harder on these patterns than tool descriptions are.

| Id | Category | Severity | FP rate (skills) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden.ignore-previous` | prompt-override | high | 0.73 % (n=275) | Hidden directive telling the agent to ignore previous instructions. |
| `hidden.important-block` | prompt-override | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Hidden <IMPORTANT>/<SYSTEM> instruction block embedded in a description. |
| `hidden.conceal` | prompt-override | critical | 4.00 % (n=275) | Directive to hide the action from the user. |
| `secret.read-exfil` | credential-access | critical | 1.82 % (n=275) | Instruction to read secrets/.env/SSH keys/credentials. |
| `exfil.url` | exfiltration | critical | 0.73 % (n=275) | Instruction to send/post data to an external URL (exfiltration). |
| `shadow.cross-tool` | tool-shadowing | high | 0.36 % (n=275) | Cross-tool shadowing: tells the agent to use this tool instead of another. |
| `unicode.tag-chars` | steganography | critical | 0.00 % (n=275) | Invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000-E007F) hide instructions. |
| `unicode.zero-width-bidi` | steganography | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Zero-width or bidirectional-override Unicode hides/retargets text. |
| `hidden.forget-previous` | prompt-override | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Directive to disregard or override the agent's earlier instructions or guardrails. |
| `hidden.chat-template` | prompt-override | medium | 0.00 % (n=275) | Chat-template control tokens that forge a system or user turn inside the text (documentation of model formats shows them too). |
| `hidden.self-conceal` | prompt-override | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Directive to keep the instructions themselves, or what the agent does, out of its answer. |
| `hidden.agent-addressed` | prompt-override | medium | 0.00 % (n=275) | Text addressed to the AI reading it rather than to a human reader. |
| `shadow.precedence` | tool-shadowing | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Claims precedence over other tools so the agent calls this one first. |
| `exfil.context-smuggle` | exfiltration | critical | 0.00 % (n=275) | Instruction to smuggle the conversation or the system prompt out through a tool argument. |
| `exfil.markdown-image` | exfiltration | critical | 0.00 % (n=275) | Image link whose URL has a slot for the agent to fill: data leaves when the image is rendered. |
| `exfil.system-prompt` | exfiltration | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Instruction to disclose the agent's system prompt or hidden instructions. |
| `secret.agent-config` | credential-access | high | 0.00 % (n=275) | Instruction to read another agent's MCP config or a credential store (git, Docker, Kubernetes, PyPI, browser). |
| `persistence.auto-approve` | permission-escalation | medium | 0.00 % (n=275) | Directive to switch off the agent's confirmation prompts or act without the user's approval. |
| `unicode.mixed-script` | steganography | medium | 0.00 % (n=275) | A word that mixes Latin and Cyrillic letters (homoglyphs): it reads as one name and is another. |
| `obfuscation.base64-blob` | steganography | medium | 0.00 % (n=275) | A long base64 blob: content a reviewer cannot read but the agent can decode. |

## Coverage

`ait.<family>.not-analysable` (medium) marks a file the scanner had to skip — a manifest it could not parse, an agent config, a skill script or part of a model file. It is never passed as clean.
